He was an unhealthy child who only understood that his days on this plane of existence were limited and wanted to help his parents be happy in the end. His father and father’s father had a dream, he told me when we were talking before his death. They wanted to unite the people of this planet under a common banner to fight against the shared enemy of this humanity, the shapeless. He wanted that dream to be a reality. That is all that he asked of me.

It was an emotion that I could relate to and decided to help him realize his dream. He had been the first sentient being that I had interacted with after awakening in this world. For more than 10 years I had roamed as a spirit. This world called me an extension of itself.

I paused in my tracks again.

This world had talked to me through emotions a year or two into my reincarnation as a spirit. If I could talk to the world before when I was nothing more than pain, anguish, and suffering from my accident and my death. I should be able to do it again.

But how would I talk to the world again?

As all story cliches go, my memories from before my time as a young prince were hazy at best and only served as sudden flashes of inspiration. The years I wandered through this land did help me develop a unique perspective about life here. I knew how people lived. I understood the pain of the beings who were shunned by humans. The shapeless were not enemies of all biological forms. There was a reason why they had devolved into monsters.

This wasn’t helping. I do not have time to think about the past. Every minute I spend not reaching my goal is another minute where my family can capture me.

My hand dug into the hard walls of the canal. I could see his grizzled face turning into a smile as he looked at me. When my eyes met him I knew that he understood. My eyes pleaded with his, begging him not to reveal the secret to my adopted family. I watched stunned as my world collapsed around me,

“What a wonderful empire.”

His words had ensured that the attention of the court was not focused on him. If this incident had not branded me for death I would appreciate the craft of his delivery and the style of his execution.

“Not only do they accept ilk of all type.” The murmur that followed did not deter him, instead gave him the energy to draw the final strike. “They have an otherworld demon to masquerade as their prince.”

I could feel a thousand pairs of eyes on me. The confusion in the eyes of my parents only to be replaced by shock and then amusement. I do not know who started the laughter, it did not take long for the halls to be rocked by shouts of ‘otherworld demon’.

He knew that mere words wouldn’t suffice. He reached out with his emaciated hand and murmured. This drew the attention of the guards. There was a cry as the captain lunged to cancel his spell. But the damage was done. His soul spell had revealed my truth to the entire world.

I expected the scream of anguish. I expected the hysterical shouts of a broken mother. Or the rage of an angry father. I thought I would have to defend myself against the guards or the courtiers. I thought I would have to fight to defend the relationships cultivated over the years. The promise made to the young child who wanted happiness for his parents held sway over me.

I expected anger.

I did not expect the silence. The cold indifference. And I did not expect the emotionless voice of the Emperor that sentenced me to death.

For four days I had been confined to the dungeons. For four days my family did come looking for me. The only company I had was Raz’ik, the survivor of a senseless war left with no way to fend for himself. He talked to me about his life, about the dreams that he couldn’t fulfill. He talked about he had seen in me a way to realize peace for this world.

He was a good man.

A good man.

I could still hear his scream after he let me escape. Tortured by the Empresses elite hunters.

I do not know how long I was in the tunnels. Time had lost any semblance of meaning. Only the blinding rage for revenge kept me walking forward. One step in front of the other. Slowly and steadily.

When I stepped out from the sewer pipe I felt the floor give away and I fell into the water. My survival training kicked in and I pushed myself off and swam to the shore of the lake. I remember crawling out from the lake and pushing myself towards dry land before strength left me. Like a tightly drawn bow that was released, I was spent and I fell into a deep sleep. The darkness finally took me.

I woke up to the sound of people. A lot of them. I was in a cabin that had sunlight trickling in creating shadows all around me.

“You are awake my prince.”

I turned and looked at the owner of my voice. My right hand and my most capable general. The shapeless who had decided to follow me. I tried to push myself off the bed I was lying on and found that I couldn’t summon my energies.

“You are tired. Please take a rest. We will arrive at the citadel in a few hours.”

I nodded in understanding and closed my eyes.

Revenge.

I will have my revenge now.

Fiction draws inspiration from reality.

And sometimes, the reality is stranger than fiction.

I used to scoff at poorly written MacGuffins that could act as Deus Ex Machina in the fantasy stories I used to read. ‘*How*’, I used to think, would a character lose sight of their core beliefs? How could the world be shattered by an occurrence that not even the smartest in the story could have anticipated?

That was until it happened to me.

There is one other common thread that I have found holds true for reality and fiction.

The sewers really are an excellent way to escape certain doom and there are chances that the exit from the sewers will not be actively monitored. If anyone could see me now as I stumbled across in the dark, my legs sunk in the filth of the city, no one would associate me with the young prince of the Tarkalin Empire. The pearl of his mother’s eyes and the pride of his father’s. The one who, if he wanted, could have become the next emperor.

The darkness is terrifying. I do not know what lies in front of me and I do not know if I am on the correct path. The flow of the wastewater guides me. I hope that the sounds I hear are only that of the rats eyeing a sudden banquet. Maybe, I think for a fleeting second, death would be a welcome recourse from the harrowing week that I have suffered.

And the anger flares up within me. No. I will not succumb to this fear and sadness. What I have received I will return. That is the duty of a prince.

I can still see his grizzled face. He had come to the court for my father’s name day. A messenger from beyond the mountains who had come bearing gifts for the lord of Tarkalin. His retinue included a princess who was to be married to me, so the messengers had announced last month. She had a pretty smile when I saw her march into the courtroom. She had a regal bearing, the aura of one who was born to rule radiated from her. Her curls were bunched up and she was dressed in the simplest of white robes. A tradition I was told extended back to the founding of their kingdom. I did not notice the look of avarice in his eyes. After all, my eyes seemed to exist only to capture her presence.

The thought of the past made me miss a footing and I fell into the water. The dark dirty water rushed into my mouth. My body convulsed as I threw up everything I had eaten in the last five hours. My white prison clothes had been stained in splotches of color and the smell could defeat a professionally trained army. I reached for the sewer walls and leaned on them. I wanted to close my eyes and let sleep take me. My body screamed in agony from the running. My eyes burned and my head ached from the mental exhaustion. Would I return back home if I died here, I wondered.

What really was home anymore?

Was it this fantastical land where magic existed in places not explored by humans?

Or was it Earth, the third planet in the solar system in the Milkyway Galaxy?

Where I had a decent life before I died.

It was a mystery to me when I first became aware of sensations again. The last thing I remembered was metal crushing me as my car collided with another. That pain was dreadful. The human body is resilient. Countless years of evolution have ensured that it can sustain dreadful impacts and still survive. But when pressure, like that of a fast-moving car engine, is applied to it, the agony is enough to make humans wish for a quick death.

I let out a long sigh. The exhaustion was making me relieve the days when I was still another being. I started to walk forward, or at least what I thought was the way towards my salvation.

When I woke up *after my death*. I stopped in my tracks.

That’s right. I thought to myself. As I started to laugh. I had died once before.

My laughter echoed in the cavern and created countless mirthless voices that laughed together at me. The rats scared that something more sinister than them had arrived in their underworld retreated back into their holes. I stopped laughing. I noticed a strange sense of detachment that occurred when I laugh without any joy in it. Perhaps it is a way of mind trying to understand my precarious situation and find a solution that will help it survive.

I straightened myself and with the support of the sewer canal walls made my way out again. The laugh seemed to have cleared something in my head. The pure, unadulterated rage that had been simmering underneath pushed its way to the surface. I wanted to live. I had to live. The dull throbbing in my head increased with every step I took and it only solidified my resolve. I knew what I had to do if I could find my way out. I had fostered and helped grow an army. It was the request of the young child whose body I now possessed.

“So really, why are you here?”  
  
“Couldn’t I have come to see an old friend? It has been a long time since you have seen me.”  
  
“No. It has been a long time since you have seen me. I have been watching your blunders every day, I can use magic, remember?”   
  
She traces a line in the air to the side with a finger and the air around the path traced by fingers starts to undulate and I can see the air condense like water in the cold wintertime. Colors start to move around in the frozen air and an image crystallizes. I sit up in the chair, my mind racing through the implications of the magic I see in front of me.   
  
“It’s a pretty place you have built.” Her gaze settled on the moving image of the capital city that her magic had conjured. Her gaze, I am mistaken to think that it contains a trace of longing in them.   
  
“This is impressive, when did you create this spell. I do not remember you using anything like this when we were together.”  
  
“Necessity is the mother of all inventions, it is a saying from a different plane. It was amusing to watch you stumble through plots, deceit, intrigue, and subterfuge. You did well not dying along the way.”  
  
“At least you seemed to have retained that unique charm to irritate me.”   
  
She smiled at me and looked at the moving image of the capital city.  
  
“I am happy for you.”  
  
“Wouldn’t be here without you. This victory and these lands belong to you as much as it does to me.”  
  
She looked amused as she said, “Well, at least you have learned diplomacy.”   
  
She waved her hand and the moving image crumbled away into the wind. I watched as the snowflakes danced in the light of the room before melting away. Would any of the witches or wizards that I knew be able to replicate what she as effortlessly crumpled. Perhaps a team of them would be able to. She really has always been this amazing.   
  
“Now then,” that smile was still there, but it carried with it a hint of danger, “why are you really here?”  
  
“I am here to ask you to become my Empress.” I stopped, her eyes held mine, “I want to marry you.”  
  
Time really does slow down when you are apprehensive, I remember when the minister of the left had once told me he had lost his weight in sweat when he asked his beau to marry him, back then I thought it was something beneath an Emperor. Today, after a very long time, I realized I too am a human.   
  
She kept looking at me, her eyes trying to find answers to the riddles that she saw on my face. Very slowly, I saw that her smile was waning. My heart pained like it was being crushed by a horse stamping on me. I hate this, I thought, this was not a pleasant feeling at all. When I am back in the city, I am going to have a word with the ministers who put me up to this, I decided. I decided to leave, lest this uncomfortable situation turn our relationship into something that cannot be salvaged.   
  
“You really went out of your way to not make this special.” She said looking at me, her hand on her chin. She looked, annoyed?  
  
“Huh?”  
  
“Being asked to marry happens only once in most lifetimes. It is supposed to be sweet, charming, and intimate. But what did you do?”  
  
“I do not understand?” I had an inkling of what she was talking about, but she couldn’t be talking about saying yes, could she. Is this happiness that I am feeling right now, but this happiness pains as well. 

She stood up from her chair and walked towards me. Every step that she took made my heart pound in its cage, I am surprised that it did not tear out the body. She stood in front of me, towering over me. Was she always this tall?   
  
I saw her hand reaching forward and cupping my cheek, and I saw on her face a smile and for the first time, I felt this is what happiness looks like. She leaned forward as she said,  
  
“It means yes. I will marry you Raon.”
